notes:
Lead profile: small engineering team (10 engs on ML/dev), product-first, building a smart help desk and in-app assistant. Main pain: inconsistent response times from Hosted API during afternoon spikes; customers in EU also see elevated RTT. They signed up self-serve, started with default region (us-east-1) and single-threaded client. They are cost-aware but willing to pay for stable latency.

Call notes / raw snippets: - 'We love the API simplicity but some chats take too long; users complain.' - 'Most sessions are short (1-3 turns) but individual prompts can hit ~2.5k tokens when users paste long docs.' - 'If we switch region, will we need code changes?'

Perf observations (from SE): - median token latency ok (200-350ms) for small prompts; p95 spikes correlated with longer prompt lengths and larger model selections. - network RTT to EU users adding 120-180ms extra; no cross-region routing currently configured on their client. - timeouts were left at default 30s; frontend unwraps errors badly (UX shows long spinner then hard error).

Recommended quick wins provided to customer: - Region choice: route EU traffic to eu-west-1 (or nearest) via API region override; no SDK code changes beyond endpoint selection. - Timeouts: set client read timeout to 10s for streaming endpoints + 45s global retry budget for occasional long generations; implement short-circuit UI after 6s with partial response fallback. - Prompt guidance: trim system + user messages; enforce a 1k token pre-trim soft-limit, summarize pasted docs before send, and use embeddings for large-doc retrieval. - Batching: enable simple request coalescing for high-throughput background tasks (embeddings) but keep chat requests single-shot for latency. - Monitoring: enable token-level latency in Console, add alert on p95>1.2s, and capture top prompt/sketch for regression hunting.

POC ask: grant a short burst of dedicated capacity credits or temporary higher concurrency limit to reproduce peak; customer prefers not to run private deployment at this stage.
